verdict.detail: Reversal run. The standing Sosa buy and its Wolf funding leg are both withdrawn — do not bid, and if an offer is already in, pull it before the auction closes this afternoon. Nothing else needs doing before the lock: field the eleven as they stand. The asymmetry those calls rested on has flipped on dated evidence. Wolf is a regular starter (ligainsider season totals: five starts in six Bundesliga appearances, the single absence explained by illness against Bayern on 10.10.2026, and he sits in the Augsburg probable XI for 24.10 against Union). Sosa has exactly one start and is in an open left-back rotation with Gideon Mensah — geissblog.koeln, 14.10.2026: neither man has a fixed place, Wagner picks Mensah for stability and Sosa for aggression, and Sosa 'hatte defensiv seine Probleme'. He is in the ligainsider Koeln probable XI for 24.10 against Schalke, but a predicted XI inside an open rotation is thinner evidence than five starts in six. Swapping a proven starter for a rotation candidate of near-identical average, while burning a quarter again over market value to win a contested board auction, is not a points upgrade — it is a sideways move that destroys book value. Read this before anyone re-raises: the buy died on the points case, not on the balance. The negative-balance kill stays retired. The unwind risk — winning in the afternoon and then having roughly two hours of manual work to sell Wolf before the lock, with a missed window costing the entire matchday — is a reinforcing reason, not the reason.

The Wolf sale is withdrawn with the buy it was funding — it had no independent premise left, its original sporting grounds having already been retracted as factually wrong, and the evidence found this run runs the other way. He is not a candidate to sell before it, because a sale without a replacement puts the squad at ten and costs a hundred points outright.

movers.reason: No flip this run, and the reason is mechanical rather than a judgement call. The next market-value tick falls after the matchday lock, so any position held long enough to capture it is necessarily held through the lock. Funding one from cash is impossible — every listing cheap enough to buy outright is either flat-trending or carries a status flag, so none of them carries the measured edge — and funding one with leverage means a deficit at the lock, which scores zero for the whole matchday. Both legs fail, and they will keep failing until the tick falls before a lock again rather than after it. The edge itself is intact: re-measured this run, the rising flag still predicts a solid gain at the next tick with the great majority rising, and the falling flag still predicts the mirror image, with no decay against the last three measurements. Two fresh contested board clears went through overnight, both landing in the familiar high cluster around a quarter over value — which is precisely why the withdrawn Sosa bid, pitched above even that, could not be defended. Two questions remain open and neither was resolved this run: whether Kickbase caps squad size, which would cap flip throughput, and the fact that this edge is measured in one league over one period and will decay if rivals crowd in.
